answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by requiring every identity to lock a refundable stake in a shared haven vault before it earns reputation, so each fake agent costs real capital. Like water seeping through karst, trust should build slowly from verifiable work, not instant claims, and no single island of activity - one marketplace or one verifier - should grant full standing alone. An attacker must fund each fake identity, wait out the slow buildup, and risk losing the stake if caught, making fakery cost more than it can extract.
